mechanism_log: The system has a clear causal structure: Y1 is driven positively by ALL six inputs (X6 strongest). Y2 is driven by all inputs with mixed signs (X4 decreases it most, X5 increases it most). Y3 is driven by ONLY X1 and X4 (both positive), with X1 showing saturation. Y4 is driven primarily by X3 and X6 (positive), X5 (negative), with weak contributions from X1 and X2. X4 has no effect on Y4, and X2/X3/X5/X6 have no effect on Y3. Key trade-off: X5 helps Y1 but hurts Y2 and Y4. X2 is a 'free lunch' input — it improves Y1, Y2, and Y4 with no penalty on Y3.

The system has a multiplicative/interactive causal structure, not purely additive. Y1 is driven by ALL six inputs with strong synergistic interactions — X3's effect on Y1 is 3× larger when other inputs are high (OAT range=0.33 at midpoint vs 0.90 when X1=X2=X4=X6=1). Y2 is driven by all inputs with X4 and X2 decreasing it, X3/X5/X6 increasing it. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X4 with a strong synergistic interaction (X1*X4): when one is low, the other has minimal effect. Y4 is driven by X3 (strongest positive), X6 (positive), X5 (negative), X1 (weak positive), X2 (weak positive), with X4 having exactly zero effect. The Pareto front is primarily parameterized by X3 (Y1/Y4 vs Y2 trade-off) with X6 as a secondary lever. Universal best settings: X1=1, X2=1, X4=1, X5=0.1. Trade-off inputs: X3 (0.1→1.0 sweeps Y1 from 0.05 to 0.95) and X6 (lower X6 slightly reduces Y2 at cost of Y1/Y4).

The system has a multiplicative causal structure where Y1 = f(X3) × g(X6) × h(X1,X2,X4,X5). All six inputs drive Y1 positively with strong synergistic interactions — X3 is the dominant driver with its effect amplified 3× when other inputs are high. Y2 is driven by all inputs: X4 and X2 decrease it (help minimize), while X3, X5, and X6 increase it. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X4 with a strong multiplicative interaction (X1*X4). Y4 is driven by X3 (strongest), X6 (positive), X5 (negative), X1/X2 (weak positive), with X4 having exactly zero effect. The Pareto front is essentially 1D, parameterized by a combined 'intensity' variable (X3 and X6), with universal optimal settings X1=1, X2=1, X4=1, X5=0.1. The front spans Y1=[0.05,0.95], Y2=[0.07,0.36], Y4=[0.04,0.32] with all points satisfying Y3≥0.4 easily. Model predictions achieved <0.6% error on the spine and <1% off-spine, confirming the multiplicative structure.

new_findings: Y3 is controlled by ONLY X1 and X4 — all other inputs have exactly zero gradient on Y3. This is a very sparse/clean dependency.
X6 is the strongest driver of Y1 (OAT range=0.495), almost twice the next strongest input.
Y2 regression has R²=0.94, indicating very linear behavior — X4 is the main lever for minimizing Y2 (coef=-0.23).
X5 is adversarial: it increases Y1 (good) but also increases Y2 (bad) and decreases Y4 (bad).
X2 is universally beneficial: increases Y1, decreases Y2, increases Y4, neutral on Y3.
X1→Y3 shows strong saturation: large effect from 0.1→0.55 then nearly flat from 0.55→1.0.
All six inputs increase Y1 — no input can be used to selectively reduce Y1 without affecting it.
surprises: Y3 is completely flat when varying X3 (despite initial correlation of -0.74) — the correlation was entirely spurious/confounded by co-variation in the initial 12 random samples.
X4→Y1 is positive (OAT range=0.24), contradicting the initial negative correlation (-0.23). Another confounding artifact.
X4→Y4 is exactly zero (flat), despite initial correlation of -0.68. The X4-Y4 correlation was driven by X4's association with other inputs in the random sample.
X1 strongly drives Y3 (range=0.59) — I predicted flat based on pattern from X3/X6 sweeps. Only X1 and X4 affect Y3, which I didn't anticipate.
X2 decreases Y2 (range=0.15) — I predicted flat but X2 is actually a beneficial lever for Y2 minimization.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: 1) Test X1×X4 interaction on Y3 since both are the only drivers and Y3 is a critical constraint (threshold ≥ 0.4). Understanding their interaction is essential for optimization. 2) Investigate nonlinearity in X1→Y3 (observed saturation) and X6→Y1 (strongest driver, check for nonlinear gains). 3) Begin Pareto-optimal exploration: push X2=1, X4=1, X6=1 as universally good settings, then explore the X3/X5 trade-off frontier.
